idea: How to prevent bad smells from drains
title: Understanding the P-Trap Water Seal to Prevent Drain Odours
description: Every fixture in your home relies on a P-trap—the curved pipe located underneath sinks, showers, and floor drains. This curve holds a small standing reservoir of water that creates a continuous liquid seal between the main drainage system and your living space. If a drain goes unused for several weeks, this trapped water slowly evaporates. Once the water level drops below the trap dip, sewer gases flow freely into the room. If a rarely used room smells like sewage, run water down every drain for 30 seconds to restore the water barrier before assuming there is a major plumbing failure.
image_prompt: A detailed 3D technical cutaway illustration of a standard white PVC P-trap assembly installed beneath a sink cabinet, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. The P-trap is rendered in a realistic cross-section view showing clean standing water filling the lower curved bend up to the weir level. The water forms a complete physical seal, separating the dry upper tailpiece from the downstream waste pipe. The background is a clean, neutral studio workshop environment with soft professional lighting highlighting the pipe wall thickness and water boundary. Photorealistic textures, realistic pipe geometry, center-focused composition, no text, no visual annotations, no visual overlays, no logos, no watermarks.
visual_story: The visual displays a realistic cross-section of a P-trap underneath a sink. Viewers can see how standing water rests in the curved dip of the pipe. The water fills the dip completely, forming an airtight barrier that prevents air from the downstream sewer pipe from passing through to the open sink drain above.

on_image_text.hook: Why Unused Drains Start to Smell Bad
on_image_text.explanation: Standing water in the P-trap forms an airtight liquid seal that blocks sewer gases from entering your home.
on_image_text.takeaway: Periodically run water down rarely used drains to keep the water barrier intact.
